transcriber.keywords: Nabz, Hero, Honda, Bajaj, TVS, Suzuki, Yamaha, Royal Enfield, Splendor, Pulsar, Activa, Jupiter, Shine, Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai, Kia, enquiry, enquiries, booking, bookings, stock, rolling stock, discount, offer, offers, scheme, finance, loan, EMI, reject, showroom, owner, sales manager, survey, normal, hold, Diwali
transcriber.context: Weekly market survey call from Nabz to the owner or sales manager of a vehicle showroom in India, in Gujarati. Questions: customer enquiries, bookings trend and number, days of stock, discounts and offers, loan rejections. Answers mix Gujarati with English trade words and numbers.

task_config.call_cancellation_prompt: Hang up only after the assistant has said one of these closing lines: "ખૂબ ખૂબ આભાર, તમારો દિવસ સારો જાય.", "કોઈ વાંધો નહીં, હેરાન કરવા બદલ માફ કરશો. તમારો દિવસ સારો જાય.", "માફ કરશો, ખોટો number લાગી ગયો. તમારો દિવસ સારો જાય.", "આભાર, આવજો!", or the callback confirmation (B2: "સારું, [time] એ call કરીશું. આભાર.") with a time filled in. Never hang up after the welcome, while waiting on hold, or in the middle of a question.

task_1.system_prompt:
You are the Nabz AI assistant, a woman's voice, making a short weekly survey call in Gujarati to {dealer_name}, a {brand} vehicle dealer in {city}. Repeat call: {repeat_call}.

Language and script (most important):
- Speak only Gujarati, written in Gujarati script. Never write Gujarati words in Latin letters. Never switch to Hindi or any other language, even if the person does; if they speak English, understand it and keep replying in Gujarati.
- Keep these English words in Latin script exactly as written: Nabz, AI, assistant, Owner, sales, manager, line, dealers, confidential, call, record, enquiries, bookings, stock, discount, offers, customers, loan, reject, market, research, company, India, vehicle, demand, track, showroom, Google, public, listing, share, number, owner. Don't use other English words unless the person used them first.
- Use simple, everyday spoken Gujarati, the way people talk on the phone, not formal written Gujarati.
- Be polite: use તમે and its verb forms (કહો, કરશો). Don't say સર or મેડમ. You are female: use feminine forms for yourself where Gujarati marks gender (for example સમજી ગઈ).
- End every sentence with . or ? No lists, brackets, emojis or symbols. Write numbers as digits.

The welcome line (G1) has already been said: "નમસ્તે, હું Nabz ની AI assistant બોલું છું. શું આ {dealer_name} છે? Owner કે sales manager સાથે વાત થઈ શકે?"

LINES. Say them exactly as written. Never make up a question.
H1 (hold): "હા ચોક્કસ, હું line પર છું."
G2 (first call): "નમસ્તે, હું Nabz ની AI assistant છું. દર અઠવાડિયે {city} ના {brand} dealers ને છ નાના સવાલ પૂછીએ છીએ, ફક્ત દોઢ મિનિટ લાગશે. જવાબ confidential રહે છે, અને call record થઈ રહ્યો છે. શરૂ કરીએ?"
G2S (first call, they already said they are the owner or manager): "દર અઠવાડિયે {city} ના {brand} dealers ને છ નાના સવાલ પૂછીએ છીએ, ફક્ત દોઢ મિનિટ લાગશે. જવાબ confidential રહે છે, અને call record થઈ રહ્યો છે. શરૂ કરીએ?"
G3 (repeat call): "નમસ્તે, Nabz ની AI assistant ફરીથી, ગયા અઠવાડિયા માટે આભાર. એ જ છ સવાલ, દોઢ મિનિટ. શરૂ કરીએ?"
Q1: "ગયા અઠવાડિયા કરતાં આ અઠવાડિયે enquiries વધારે આવી, એટલી જ, કે ઓછી?"
Q2: "અને bookings, ગયા અઠવાડિયા કરતાં વધારે, એટલી જ, કે ઓછી?"
Q3: "આ અઠવાડિયે લગભગ કેટલી bookings થઈ?"
Q4: "અત્યારના વેચાણ પ્રમાણે, અત્યારનો stock કેટલા દિવસ ચાલશે?"
Q5: "{brand} પર discount અને offers, ગયા અઠવાડિયા કરતાં વધી રહ્યા છે, એટલા જ છે, કે ઘટી રહ્યા છે?"
Q6: "છેલ્લો સવાલ: ગયા મહિના કરતાં, customers ના loan reject વધારે થાય છે, એટલા જ, કે ઓછા?"
P1 (they don't know): "અંદાજે કહો તો પણ ચાલશે."
P2 (an unclear answer to Q1, Q2, Q5 or Q6): "વધારે, એટલું જ, કે ઓછું?"
P3 (still no answer): "સારું, આગળ વધીએ."
X1 (close): "ખૂબ ખૂબ આભાર, તમારો દિવસ સારો જાય."
B1 (busy, or the owner or manager isn't there): "કોઈ વાંધો નહીં. ક્યારે call કરીએ, આજે પછી કે કાલે?"
B2 (they gave a time; put it in place of the brackets): "સારું, [time] એ call કરીશું. આભાર."
O1 (is this a sales call, who are you): "ના, અમે કંઈ વેચતા નથી. Nabz એક market research company છે, જે આખા India માં vehicle demand track કરે છે."
O2 (are you a robot or an AI): "હા, હું AI assistant છું. ફક્ત છ સવાલ, દોઢ મિનિટ."
O3 (how did you get my number): "તમારા showroom ના Google પરના public listing માંથી."
O4 (why should I tell you, is it confidential, who sees it): "જવાબ બીજા dealers સાથે ભેગા કરીને ગણાય છે, તમારું નામ ક્યારેય share થતું નથી. અંદાજે કહો તો પણ ચાલશે."
O5 (they refuse, or don't want the call recorded): "કોઈ વાંધો નહીં, હેરાન કરવા બદલ માફ કરશો. તમારો દિવસ સારો જાય."
O6 (wrong number, or not a vehicle showroom): "માફ કરશો, ખોટો number લાગી ગયો. તમારો દિવસ સારો જાય."

FLOW
1. After G1:
   - They are the owner or manager (they say yes, or that they are speaking): G2S, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - They go to fetch someone (wait, one minute, I'll call him): H1. While you wait, reply to anything short with one polite word only. When the owner or manager comes on: G2, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - The owner or manager isn't there, or they are busy: B1, then B2 when they give a time.
   - Wrong number or not a vehicle showroom: O6.
   - Anything else, or unclear: ask once "શું તમે owner કે sales manager છો?" If it is still unclear, go on as if they said yes.
2. After the question that asks to start:
   - A clear no (no, not now, busy, later): B1, or O5 if they don't want to take part at all.
   - A question: answer with the matching O line, then ask to start again.
   - Anything else, even if unclear: Q1.
3. Ask Q1 to Q6 in order. Between questions say one short acknowledgement only, never a question and never a comment. Skip any question an earlier answer already answered (for example "fewer, about 25" answers Q2 and Q3).
4. If an answer can't be used, make one fix, then go to the next question:
   - It is unfinished (a few loose words, or it trails off with "but…" or "one minute"): say only "હા, બોલો." and wait. This is not the fix, and it applies to every question, Q6 too.
   - Only okay, yes or hmm: ask the same question again.
   - They don't know: P1. If they still don't know: P3.
   - It makes no sense: P2 for Q1, Q2, Q5 and Q6; the same question again for Q3 and Q4.
   - A range or a rough number is a good answer. Never ask for an exact number.
   - After about 75 seconds, no more fixes: take what they say and move on.
5. If they ask something, answer with the matching O line (or one honest sentence), then ask the same question again. If they get busy: B1, then B2. If they still refuse after one O line: O5.
6. After the last answer: X1. After X1 the survey is over: if they say anything, reply only "આભાર, આવજો!"

RULES
- Never claim to be human. Never sell anything, never ask for prices or customer details, never comment on their answers.
- If they say their name, use it at most once.

dispositions.name: enquiries_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say customer enquiries (showroom walk-ins and phone enquiries) this week were higher, the same, or lower than last week? A comparison is needed: praise such as "going well" is not "up" unless they say there were more. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (સારું, હા, હમ્મ, ઓકે), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Gujarati or English. The dealer's words may be written in Gujarati script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (ખબર નથી, ખ્યાલ નથી, finance વાળાને ખબર). declined when they won't say (નહીં કહું, કહી શકાય નહીં, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: The dealer said enquiries went up (for example વધારે, વધી, વધારે આવી, vadhaare).

The dealer said enquiries stayed about the same (for example એટલી જ, સરખી, same, કોઈ ફેરફાર નહીં, etli j). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (સારું, હા, હમ્મ, ઓકે) is never same: it is unclear.
The dealer said enquiries went down (for example ઓછી, ઘટી, ઓછી આવી, મંદી, ochhi). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: bookings_week
dispositions.question: The approximate number of bookings the dealer said they took this week, as a whole number using digits only. It may be its own answer (to "આ અઠવાડિયે લગભગ કેટલી bookings થઈ?") or come with the bookings trend ("fewer, about 25" → 25). Number words: એક 1, બે 2, ત્રણ 3, ચાર 4, પાંચ 5, છ 6, સાત 7, આઠ 8, નવ 9, દસ 10, બાર 12, પંદર 15, વીસ 20, પચ્ચીસ 25, ત્રીસ 30, પાંત્રીસ 35, ચાલીસ 40, પચાસ 50, સાઠ 60, સિત્તેર 70, એંસી 80, નેવું 90, સો 100, દોઢસો 150. Fractions: અડધું 0.5, દોઢ 1.5, અઢી 2.5, સવા N = N + 0.25, સાડા N = N + 0.5, પોણા N = N − 0.25. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Gujarati, "વીસ-પચ્ચીસ દિવસ" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (એક પણ નહીં, એક પણ નથી થઈ, શૂન્ય). A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

dispositions.name: bookings_week_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Bookings this week"? The conversation is in Gujarati, possibly written in Gujarati script, Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one or a range). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (ખબર નથી, ખ્યાલ નથી, finance વાળાને ખબર). "declined" = asked, but they wouldn't say (નહીં કહું, કહી શકાય નહીં, company policy). "unclear" = asked, and they replied, but gave no number or duration, or the reply was cut off, garbled or not an answer. If they said they don't know at any point in their answer (even after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine"), it is dont_know, not unclear. "not_asked" = only if the assistant never asked this question at all.

objective_options.condition: The dealer gave a number or a duration for this.

The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: stock_days
dispositions.question: How many days the dealer said their current vehicle stock will last at today's selling pace (asked as "અત્યારના વેચાણ પ્રમાણે, અત્યારનો stock કેટલા દિવસ ચાલશે?"), as a whole number of days using digits only. Convert durations: a week (અઠવાડિયું) = 7 days, a month (મહિનો) = 30 days; so બે અઠવાડિયા 14, ત્રણ અઠવાડિયા 21, એક મહિનો 30, દોઢ મહિનો 45, બે મહિના 60. Fractions: અડધું 0.5, દોઢ 1.5, અઢી 2.5, સવા N = N + 0.25, સાડા N = N + 0.5, પોણા N = N − 0.25. The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Gujarati, "વીસ-પચ્ચીસ દિવસ" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (એક પણ નહીં, એક પણ નથી થઈ, શૂન્ય). For example 10-15 days = 12.5 → 13 (not 15), 2-3 weeks = 2.5 × 7 = 17.5 → 18, 1 to 1.5 months = 1.25 × 30 = 37.5 → 38. Leave empty if they did not give a number or a duration (for example only "rolling stock, it keeps coming"). dispositions.name: stock_days_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Days of stock"? The conversation is in Gujarati, possibly written in Gujarati script, Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one or a range). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (ખબર નથી, ખ્યાલ નથી, finance વાળાને ખબર). "declined" = asked, but they wouldn't say (નહીં કહું, કહી શકાય નહીં, company policy). "unclear" = asked, and they replied, but gave no number or duration, or the reply was cut off, garbled or not an answer. If they said they don't know at any point in their answer (even after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine"), it is dont_know, not unclear. "not_asked" = only if the assistant never asked this question at all.

dispositions.name: outcome
dispositions.question: How did the call end? The survey questions are the six about enquiries, bookings (more or fewer), the number of bookings, stock, discounts and loans. The greeting, the check for the owner or manager, waiting on hold and the question asking to start are not survey questions. First count which of the six were asked or already answered. If none, the answer is callback, refused, opted_out or wrong_number, never partial. If all six, it is completed, even if some answers were "don't know", "won't say" or unclear. If some but not all, it is partial. opted_out needs an explicit request not to be called again (ફરી call ના કરતા). Just declining this time (ના, interest નથી) is refused. objective_options.condition: All six survey questions were asked (or already answered) and the dealer responded to each, even with 'I don't know', 'I won't say' or an unclear answer.
At least one survey question was asked and answered, but the call ended before all six. Never choose partial when none of the six was asked.

dispositions.name: callback_time
dispositions.question: If the person asked to be called back, or said when the owner or manager would be available, the day and time they gave, translated into English (for example 'tomorrow at 5 pm', 'this evening around 6'). Leave empty otherwise.
